utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: This Status Conference is called to order. Madam Registrar, can you call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-10-A, the Prosecutor versus Goran Jelisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, let me call for the appearances. Present for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, I'm Upawansa Yapa. I appear for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thanks. I note that for the accused -- for the appellant, Mr. Jelisic, there was an arrangement to hear counsel, Mr. Clegg, by phone link. I understand the link is difficult to establish, or may I have information on whether we can establish the link or not? Thank you, Madam Registrar. I understand it's still not possible to have Mr. Clegg on the phone, and since he is not available where he should have been, so I don't know how we should proceed now with the Status Conference. I would ask Mr. Jelisic, Mr. Jelisic, I see your counsel, Mr. Clegg, is not available on the phone link. Therefore, I would like to ask you if you want to proceed to have the Status Conference notwithstanding the absence of your counsel, because the law, the Statute, allows you to defend yourself in person, but of course, you are not requested to do it. You can say that you do not want to proceed without your counsel, I want to be quite clear on that. You may accept to proceed to the Status Conference in the absence of your counsel, but it is your full right to say that you want your counsel. In that case, we will postpone the Status Conference, adjourn it, and have it another day. Is that very clear to you, the option you have?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for allowing me to speak. I don't know what to say to you. I find myself in a very embarrassing situation. I don't know if I refuse this Status Conference whether I will give rise to problems for the Chamber and for the Registry and the Prosecution, so I leave it up to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jelisic. There will be certainly no problem in the sense that I will proceed that way: If you prefer to have the Status Conference with the assistance of your counsel, I will adjourn now and put the Status Conference on another day, trying to remain within the 120 days. I could have it on Thursday, for instance, this week, and try in the meantime to have your counsel available for that moment, your counsel or your co-counsel, I mean one of the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: So I understand you prefer to postpone the Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I leave it up to you. We Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Mr. Jelisic, I do not think that you can leave it up to me. I mean, let me try to be more specific. The Statute, in line with international human rights standards, says that the accused has the right to defend himself in person or to defend himself through the legal assistance of his counsel. Now, the choice is up to you. You have the right to be assisted by counsel, and you have the right to proceed without counsel, but the choice, I cannot make it for you. If you leave it up to me, I will not proceed in the absence of your counsel necessarily, because it's you who exercises the right to proceed without the counsel or to proceed with the counsel. I must leave it up to you, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I do not wish the Status Conference to be held without my counsel present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Jelisic. I accept that. And in that case, I will adjourn this Status Conference, but before that I think we should ask Mr. Clegg an explanation why, after having made an appointment, he didn't -- was not available at that appointment, phone link. So we should proceed that way, but I wanted to put it on record. And I will now adjourn, and I think we can have the Status Conference maybe in two or three days. Mr. Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as you have touched upon the question of Mr. Clegg, I think that at this moment Mr. Clegg is in charge of three cases and that he's ignoring my case, and that this is very irresponsible from counsel. So if you can influence him and get him to appear the next time and give an explanation, I would be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jelisic. That's exactly what I propose to do, to ask a specific explanation as to why he did not -- he's not available when he should have been now. And of course, I hope it's not the case that he's not taking care of your case. I hope not. In any case, we will have an explanation from Mr. Clegg on what happened. Maybe it's something that is outside his control. I mean, it's also possible. Well, the meeting stands -- the hearing stands adjourned, and I will make a Scheduling Order for the Status Conference.

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
